brief: A PLA dome: exactly half of a 70 mm sphere, sitting flat side to the right side, hollow on the inside. It carries no load, so there is no load case.

intent.summary: A hollow hemispherical dome, half of a 70 mm sphere, printed in PLA, oriented with its flat face to the right; stated to carry no load.
stated: Shape is exactly half of a 70 mm sphere (a hemisphere)
Oriented with the flat (cut) side facing right
Carries no load, so there is no load case
implied: Being a half-sphere with a flat side implies the flat circular face is the open/base face of the dome
Hollow interior implies the part is a shell with some wall thickness rather than solid, so a wall thickness must exist even if unspecified
PLA material implies standard FDM 3D-printing process considerations (layer lines, print orientation effects) rather than machining or casting
'Sitting flat side to the right' implies an intended orientation in use or in a drawing/assembly, suggesting the flat face may rest against or face another surface or viewer
unstated: Wall thickness of the hollow shell
Whether the flat circular face is open (a bowl-like shell) or closed with a floor/base
Whether there is a rim, lip, or flange around the open edge, and if so its dimensions
Tolerances on the 70 mm diameter and on roundness
Any mounting or fastening features (holes, bosses, snap features) if it needs to attach to anything
Wall thickness uniformity vs. draft/print-orientation constraints specific to PLA FDM printing
Any functional purpose of the hollow cavity (e.g., does it enclose another component, need ventilation, drainage, or access holes)
Operating/storage temperature range (relevant since PLA has a low heat-deflection temperature)
Whether 'no load case' excludes handling loads, shipping loads, or its own weight during printing/assembly
Quantity to be produced and whether design needs to account for print-bed size or support material
Any regulatory, safety, or certification requirements
out_of_scope: Selecting a specific wall thickness value
Choosing PLA grade/brand or print settings
Determining actual structural capacity despite 'no load' claim
risk_signals: None stated: the brief explicitly says the part carries no load; no indication of pressure containment, overhead lifting, human-carrying, or energy storage

requirements.statement: The dome's overall height (flat face to apex), oriented with its axis along X since the flat side faces right, shall equal the sphere radius of 35 mm.
requirements.rationale: With the flat cut face oriented to the right (along X), the part's extent along X is the hemisphere's radius.

requirements.statement: The dome's overall width across the circular base shall equal the 70 mm sphere diameter.
requirements.rationale: The circular base face lies in the YZ plane, so Y spans the full diameter.

requirements.statement: The dome's overall depth across the circular base shall equal the 70 mm sphere diameter.
requirements.rationale: The circular base face lies in the YZ plane, so Z spans the full diameter, matching Y for a round cross-section.

requirements.statement: The dome's geometry shall derive from a sphere of 70 mm diameter, of which it is exactly one half.

assumptions.statement: The hollow shell has a uniform wall thickness of 2 mm, a typical value for a PLA FDM print of this size.
assumptions.rationale: The brief states the dome is hollow but gives no wall thickness; 2 mm is a common default for PLA prints balancing strength and print time at this scale.
assumptions.consequence_if_wrong: A thinner wall may be too weak or print poorly with warping/layer defects; a thicker wall adds unnecessary weight and print time.

assumptions.statement: The flat circular face (the cut face of the hemisphere) is open, making the part a bowl-like shell rather than a closed hollow sphere-half.
assumptions.rationale: A 'hollow' dome with a flat side most naturally reads as an open-bottomed shell, consistent with typical dome/cover parts.
assumptions.consequence_if_wrong: If the flat face should be closed with a floor, the part would need an added base disc, changing its mass and print orientation needs.

notes: REQ_BOUNDING_BOX_X carried `source: "user"` against a threshold the brief does not state. The figure may be sound -- a derived dimension, a manufacturing limit -- but the user did not write it, so it is recorded as `derived` rather than reported back to them as their own requirement.
dropped 2 load question(s): the brief states that this part carries no load, so there was nothing to be uncertain about

answer.name: Hollow hemispherical dome
answer.description: Half of a 70 mm sphere, hollow-shelled, flat face oriented to the right (open along +X).

note: Claude Sonnet 5, 14 Oct 2026. The dome was cut in half and then shelled: a sealed hollow, reported as PASS though the brief asked for it open; the wall assumption carried no value field, so nothing checked the hollow.
